subject: Urgent: MedFlow amplified 429/5xx wave — proposed fallback & mitigation plan
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir@medflow.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anya Li <anya@medflow.ai>, MedFlow SRE <sre@medflow.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: production — intermittent streaming timeouts (429 spikes)

Ben,

We started seeing a sharp uptick in 429s and 5xxs from the Redwood API around 08:45 PT this morning. Symptoms: persistent client-side timeouts during streaming completions (clients time out at ~15s), idle-stream disconnects after ~30s, and then a flood of retries from our web clients which amplifies the error wave.

Impact: about 18% of active sessions experienced at least one truncated completion in the last hour; UX is degraded and support pages are lighting up. We collected client-side logs and attached a sampling (medflow_timeouts_logs_20280214.zip).

Can your team confirm whether this is an infrastructure autoscaler/keepalive regression or a serving runtime issue? We need a mitigation path (short-term fallback + ETA) — this is affecting a scheduled demo for a partner at 11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Samir Gupta
Head of Platform, MedFlow
[supporting logs attached: medflow_timeouts_logs_20280214.zip]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@medflow.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production — intermittent streaming timeouts (429 spikes)

Samir — thanks for the quick heads-up and the logs. I’m escalating this immediately to SRE. Initial asks: 1) Can you confirm client retry policy (max retries, backoff)? 2) Are most errors 429 or 5xx? Your logs show a mix but we need counts by code.

Immediate mitigation options we can take in the next 30–90 minutes:
- Temporarily route your traffic to our standby pool in us-west-2 (failover) to relieve regional pressure.
- Reduce client max retries via a short-lived config toggle (recommended to prevent amplification).
- Abort in-flight streaming after 25s server-side to avoid open sockets accumulating (shorter than client timeout).

I’ve looped in Priyom (SRE) and Grace (CS) to run triage and coordinate a controlled failover if you approve. We’ll also prepare an exec note and credit request if the impact is sustained.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 09:42:00 -08:00
Subject: NEXT STEPS: MedFlow 429/5xx spike — triage notes and hotfix plan

Triage summary (observed 09:30–09:40 PT):
- 429 rate rose from baseline ~0.6% to ~7.4% in a 10-minute window; concurrent 5xxs increased from 0.1% to 0.9%.
- Correlated with autoscaler activity: several GPU nodes were cycled during throughput surge => transient capacity gaps and longer latency tails for streaming endpoints.
- Idle-connection churn: K/V cache misses on warmup increased tail latency for first few tokens in a stream.

Immediate mitigations (now–60m):
1) Increase streaming keepalive interval and enable TCP-level keepalives to reduce idle disconnects. (hotpatch queued)
2) Apply temporary rate-limiter on client retries for MedFlow via per-route token bucket (drop/reject retries above threshold).
3) Circuit-breaker: fail open to a lower-capacity, smaller-quantized variant that has lower p99 latency for short completions (can be inline routed for MedFlow only).
4) Manual node warmup: cache priming for top-20 prefixes observed in logs.

Runbook links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3245 (triage) and https://dashboard.redwood.ai/incident/INC-20280214-3

I’ll kick off #3 immediately and coordinate the failover test with Ben/Grace. ETA for observable improvement: 10–25 minutes after circuit-cut. Will post progress updates to this thread.

— Priyom (SRE)
[attachment: initial_triage_snapshot.json]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@medflow.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production — intermittent streaming timeouts (429 spikes)

Samir — thanks for your patience. Priyom has a mitigation plan and is executing a targeted circuit to a lower-p99 variant. We’d like to propose a controlled failover of a portion of your traffic to our standby us-west-2 capacity for the next 2 hours to buy breathing room for the autoscaler and priming.

If you approve the partial failover we will:
- Route 30% of sessions to standby pool (can bump to 50% if stable).
- Enact retry throttling for browsers to stop amplification.
- Provide live SLO graphs and a timeline to your SRE team.

As this is customer-facing impact, I’ve looped in Lauren to pre-authorize a goodwill credit if the degradation persists beyond our incident window. Can you confirm: (a) approve failover (yes/no), (b) accept temporary session routing changes?

Grace O'Connor
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
[screenshot: slo_dashboard_snapshot.png]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Feb 2028 10:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Exec visibility: MedFlow incident — customer impacted, mitigation underway

Lauren/Jonas — FYI and asking for quick confirmation on a customer goodwill credit if the incident persists >2 hours. MedFlow is a strategic mid-market account (DEAL-4981) with a partner demo at 11:00 PT — immediate reputational risk.

Actions taken: Priyom enabled a temporary circuit-breaker to a lower-latency variant and Grace requested a partial failover (pending customer approval). Expected reduction in client timeouts within 10–25 minutes of route change.

Request: Please pre-approve a one-time credit of up to 10% of the last invoice if we cannot restore normal SLOs within 2 hours. I’ll update you with an incident timeline and the SLO snapshot (attached).

Ben

From: Samir Gupta <samir@medflow.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: MedFlow SRE <sre@medflow.ai>, Anya Li <anya@medflow.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Feb 2028 17:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: production — intermittent streaming timeouts (429 spikes)

Grace / Ben — we confirmed the partial failover and the circuit to the smaller variant this morning. Observed improvements: 429 rate reduced to ~1.1% and user-reported truncated completions dropped by ~80% during the 11:00–13:00 PT window.

We accept the temporary routing change for the remaining peak window on Friday and appreciate the proposed credit if there are any lingering issues. Please keep us apprised of a long-term mitigation (autoscaler tuning + priming) and a postmortem.

Thanks for the rapid response.
Samir
Head of Platform, MedFlow
